pressure_equipment_regulations.legislation: Pressure Equipment Regulations (PER), GNR 734 of 2009 under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993)
key_requirements: All pressure equipment manufactured, repaired, or maintained must conform to SANS 347:2000 (Categorisation and conformity assessment criteria for pressure equipment)
Manufacturers and repair contractors must hold a valid Approved Inspection Authority (AIA) registration or work under an AIA
Welding on pressure vessels must comply with ISO 3834 quality requirements for fusion welding
Imported pressure equipment bearing the ASME stamp (ASME VIII Division 1) is accepted as meeting PER requirements provided full ASME Code of Construction compliance is demonstrated
Competent Persons (CPs) for pressure equipment must be certified by the SAQCC CP certification body under the SAIW
Inspectors of Pressurised Equipment (IPEs) must be certified by SAQCC IPE
recommended_certifications: SAQCC CP and IPE personnel certification
ASME Section IX (Welding and Brazing Qualifications)
pressure_equipment_regulations.regulator: Department of Employment and Labour (via Inspection and Enforcement Services)

welding_certifications.asme_relevance: ASME Section IX applies to welding procedure qualifications (WPSs and PQRs) and welder performance qualifications (WPQs) for pressure-containing components
welding_certifications.local_certification_body: SAIW (South African Institute of Welding) â€” https://www.saiw.co.za
requirements: Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS) must be qualified per ISO 15614 or ASME IX
Welders must hold current Welder Qualification Test (WQT) certificates issued by SAIW or TÃœV Rheinland South Africa
NDT inspectors must be qualified to ASNT Level II or PCN Level 2 (per SANS 10227)
All welding records must be retained per ISO 3834-2 documentation requirements

sacpcmp_registration.legislation: Construction Industry Development Board Act (Act 38 of 2000) and Project and Construction Management Professions Act (Act 48 of 2000)
sacpcmp_registration.body: South African Council for the Project and Construction Management Professions (SACPCMP) â€” https://sacpcmp.org.za
requirements: Construction Health and Safety Officers (CHSOs) on construction sites must be registered with SACPCMP; unregistered CHSOs cannot lawfully practise
Construction Health and Safety Managers (CHSMs) responsible for project OHS files must hold SACPCMP Professional registration (Pr.CHSM)
Project Managers on CIDB-registered contracts above Grade 5 are expected to hold Pr.PM (Professional Project Manager) registration
Registration requires prescribed qualifications (relevant degree or diploma), documented experience, and a professional examination

ohs_act_obligations.legislation: Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993), with the Construction Regulations 2014 and General Machinery Regulations applying to onsite work
key_contractor_obligations: Section 37(2): Written agreement required between the client (mandator) and the contractor outlining OHS responsibilities before work commences
Construction Regulations Regulation 5: Principal contractor must prepare a detailed Health and Safety Plan (HSP) before commencing work on a construction site
Construction Regulations Regulation 6: Baseline risk assessment required for all construction activities

Onsite maintenance at mines is also subject to the Mine Health and Safety Act (Act 29 of 1996) when conducted on a mine site â€” contractors must comply with the mine's Section 11 Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS)

COID Act (Act 130 of 1993): All employees must be registered with the Compensation Fund (or an approved mutual association); letter of good standing required before site access is granted by most mining clients
Machinery operators must hold a valid Certificate of Competence issued under the Driven Machinery Regulations (DMR)
recommended_certifications: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management System (replaces OHSAS 18001)
NOSA NOSCAR or equivalent 5-Star safety rating (widely required by mining house clients as a prequalification criterion)

additional_requirements.description: Required for all contractors on government and SOE projects; Endeto should target Grade 5ME and Grade 6ME as minimum for mining maintenance contracts; upgrade path to Grade 7+ for major shutdown contracts

Mining Charter III (2018) and Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment require mining house suppliers to hold a valid B-BBEE Level 4 or better certificate; Level 1-2 provides procurement recognition points for mining clients
Engineers signing off on designs or structural calculations must be registered with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) as Professional Engineers (Pr.Eng)

When working on a mine as a contractor, Endeto must comply with Mine Health and Safety Act (Act 29 of 1996) Section 11 requirements including appointment documentation and compliance with the mine's risk management system
